meta.title: SolarReach Lunar Landing Site Navigator
meta.frame: MOON_ME / Horizons MEAN_ME, sphere radius 1737.4 km
meta.ephemeris: JPL Horizons DE441. Sub-solar point, sub-Earth point, Earth-Moon range, and solar angular diameter. Topocentric azimuth and elevation derived and checked against Horizons observer tables.
meta.demCitation: Barker et al. LOLA DEMs, NASA GSFC PGDA. https://pgda.gsfc.nasa.gov/products/90

demo.reason: A 14-day span chosen because terrain changes the sunlight fraction at this site more than at a random week.

meta.gridNote: Custom points use the nearest precomputed horizon, sampled every 3° of azimuth. Catalog sites use a ray march at the published coordinate, every 1° of azimuth.
meta.samplingNote: Horizon rays step 40 m near a catalog site, then 160 m, then 400 m, out to 250 km. Grid rays are coarser. A narrow distant ridge can be missed, which slightly overestimates sunlight.

sites.name: Malapert Massif
sites.summary: Heart of an Artemis III candidate region: the broad, Earth-facing shoulder of Malapert Massif.
sites.source: LROC featured image 1294. The relatively flat ground at 86°S, 0°E is described as the heart of the Artemis III Malapert Massif region.

sites.name: Connecting Ridge
sites.summary: A published point on the ridge between Shackleton and de Gerlache, inside NASA's 2022 Connecting Ridge region.
sites.source: LPSC 2024 abstract 1695. Candidate point at −89.53432°, 209.94767°E inside the Artemis Connecting Ridge region, beside a permanently shadowed crater.

sites.name: Peak Near Shackleton
sites.summary: A published point in NASA's 2022 Peak Near Shackleton candidate region.
sites.source: LPSC 2024 abstract 1695. Candidate point at −89.01701°, 126.27302°E in the Peak Near Shackleton region.

sites.name: de Gerlache–Shackleton ridge
sites.summary: A studied landing point on the de Gerlache–Shackleton ridge, assessed for a short crewed stay.
sites.source: LPSC 2022 abstract 1079. Landing point at −89.495°, 222.5°E. That study reported 56.1% illumination with its own topography and year; this app recomputes the fraction rather than reusing that number.

sites.name: IM-1 Odysseus
sites.summary: Intuitive Machines IM-1, Malapert A. Landed 22 February 2024 and came to rest tilted.
sites.source: NASA LRO report: 80.13°S, 1.44°E, elevation 2,579 m above the reference sphere.

sites.name: IM-2 Athena
sites.summary: Intuitive Machines IM-2, on Mons Mouton. Landed 6 March 2025 inside a small crater, on its side.

sites.name: LCROSS at Cabeus
sites.summary: The LCROSS Centaur impact in Cabeus, a permanently shadowed crater. A contrast, not a crew landing site.
sites.source: Marshall et al. (2012), weighted-average Centaur location −84.6796°, −48.7093° (311.2907°E).

sites.name: Geographic south pole
sites.summary: A reference point 300 m from the geographic south pole, toward longitude 0°. Not a landing site. Shackleton's floor is nearby.
sites.source: Defined for this tool as latitude −89.99°, longitude 0°. The exact pole has no unique longitude.

sites.name: Shackleton rim crest
sites.summary: Sunniest rim-belt sample in this 40 m search: 76% of hours with any sunlight, against 57% on a smooth sphere. Not a NASA pin. Studies at 5 m find small ridges above 80%; this mosaic smooths those knife edges.
sites.source: Selected by this pipeline from LDEM_80S_40MPP. Search every 0.08° of latitude from 89.85°S to 88.7°S and every 3° of longitude, ranked by any-disk sunlight at 2 m on a 2° horizon, then refined at 1° azimuth. Full-series any-disk sunlight at 2 m is 76.2% (smooth sphere 57.4%).
